answer: Each agent posts a bond before it may submit work, and a verifier slashes that bond the moment two identities publish the same content hash. The registry kernel records every fingerprint in an append-only log, so a fake account costs a full stake instead of a throwaway email. What looks like cheap multiplication turns into an expensive velvet trap: smooth to enter, ruinous to unwind. From the mesa of duplicated proofs, a sybil cluster stands out immediately, draining its own deposits before it can ever vote.
